title: Invariant affine shrinking around a finite saturated set
statement: Let $p:X\to Y$ be finite, flat and locally of finite presentation [def-pc-finite-locally-free], and let $V\to X$ have a transport descent datum $D$ [def-pd-descent-datum]. Let $(s,q):R\to V\times_Y X$ be a cartesian presentation [def-pc-fibre-product], with target $t:R\to V$ given by universal transport of $s$ along $s\circ(V\to X)$ and $q$. Suppose $S\subseteq V$ is finite and saturated, meaning $s^{-1}(S)=t^{-1}(S)$. For any affine open $A\subseteq V$ containing $S$, there exists an affine open $U$ with $S\subseteq U\subseteq A$ and $s^{-1}(U)=t^{-1}(U)$. The empty finite set and varying local ranks are allowed. Surjectivity of $p$ is not assumed.

source.place: Tag 03JE, proof from the affine open W to the norm nonvanishing locus

proof.text: Use the existing transport_left_naturality theorem to construct inversion and identity arrows from the transport identity and cocycle laws. Use the existing descent_orbit_saturated theorem to show that source and target have equal orbits. The source is a base change of p and inversion exchanges source and target, hence both projections are finite locally free.

Let Z=t(s^{-1}(V minus A)). It is closed since t is finite. Its complement W is invariant by composition and inversion, is contained in A by identity arrows, and contains S by saturation. Finite prime avoidance on A gives f with S contained in D(f) contained in W.

Define U to be the complement of t(s⁻¹(V minus D(f))). The proved groupoid interior argument makes U open, invariant, contained in D(f), and containing S. Inversion proves that the t-image of the s-preimage of the complement of D(f) equals the s-image of its t-preimage. Hence U equals W intersected with the latter complement. Invariance of W and W contained in A give s⁻¹(W) contained in t⁻¹(A). Apply lem-pd-descent-norm-locus-affine to this precisely specified U.
Return this affine U with the already proved containment of S, containment in A, and invariance. For S empty return the empty affine open.

theorem exists_descent_norm_affine_shrinking
    {X Y R : Scheme.{u}} {p : X ⟶ Y} {V : Over X}
    (D : Over.DescentDatum p V) (s : R ⟶ V.left) (q : R ⟶ X) (t : R ⟶ V.left)
    (hsq : IsPullback s q (V.hom ≫ p) p)
    (ht : (D.transport (s ≫ V.hom) q
      (by simpa only [Category.assoc] using hsq.w) (Over.homMk s)).left = t)
    [IsFinite p] [Flat p] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation p]
    (S : Set V.left) (hS : S.Finite) (hstable : s ⁻¹' S = t ⁻¹' S)
    (A : V.left.Opens) (hA : IsAffineOpen A) (hSA : S ⊆ A) :
    ∃ U : V.left.Opens, S ⊆ U ∧ IsAffineOpen U ∧ U ≤ A ∧ s ⁻¹' (U : Set V.left) =
      t ⁻¹' (U : Set V.left)
